ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To disclose or show something, including instruction shown in a public interview.
EvidenceBody: An unnamed monk asks Baizhang Yuansu to disclose the intention of the patriarch’s coming from the west and receives “the mud ox swallows the huge wave”; the named layman He Changbai asks Juelang Daosheng for instruction for the Fushan assembly and receives a verse about clouds and snow. In the Longtan–Tianhuang case, Longtan Chongxin complains that he has long attended without being shown the essentials of mind. Tianhuang Daowu lists raising a hand when tea was brought and lowering his head when greeted, then asks, “Where was I not showing you the essentials of mind?” (那裏不是與你開示心要處). The Blue Cliff Record's compiler narrates that Jingqing Daofu used a responsive dynamic to “show later students” (開示後學); Jingqing is the person described, not the utterer of that clause. The monastery manager Chengyi tells Jifei Ruyi that he has received Jifei’s disclosure (承師開示), treating Jifei’s reply as instruction already given. Request, act, repeated conduct, and received instruction are stages of the same showing, not different lexical referents.
